title: Translations on the Coordinate Plane Core Test
description: Translate points and figures on the coordinate plane using words, vectors, coordinate rules, and reasoning about images and preimages.

questions.questionText: Point A is at (-3, 2). It is translated 4 units right and 1 unit down. What are the coordinates of A'?
questions.explanation: A translation adds the horizontal change to x and the vertical change to y: (-3, 2) becomes (1, 1).

questions.questionText: Point A is at (1, -5). It is translated 2 units left and 3 units up. What are the coordinates of A'?
questions.explanation: A translation adds the horizontal change to x and the vertical change to y: (1, -5) becomes (-1, -2).

questions.questionText: Point A is at (0, 4). It is translated 5 units right and 2 units up. What are the coordinates of A'?
questions.explanation: A translation adds the horizontal change to x and the vertical change to y: (0, 4) becomes (5, 6).

questions.questionText: Point A is at (-6, -1). It is translated 3 units right and 4 units down. What are the coordinates of A'?
questions.explanation: A translation adds the horizontal change to x and the vertical change to y: (-6, -1) becomes (-3, -5).

questions.questionText: Point A is at (2, 2). It is translated 5 units left and 3 units down. What are the coordinates of A'?
questions.explanation: A translation adds the horizontal change to x and the vertical change to y: (2, 2) becomes (-3, -1).

questions.questionText: Point A is at (-1, 6). It is translated no horizontal move and 5 units down. What are the coordinates of A'?
questions.explanation: A translation adds the horizontal change to x and the vertical change to y: (-1, 6) becomes (-1, 1).

questions.questionText: Point A is at (4, -3). It is translated 4 units left and 4 units up. What are the coordinates of A'?
questions.explanation: A translation adds the horizontal change to x and the vertical change to y: (4, -3) becomes (0, 1).

questions.questionText: Point A is at (-5, 0). It is translated 2 units right and 6 units up. What are the coordinates of A'?
questions.explanation: A translation adds the horizontal change to x and the vertical change to y: (-5, 0) becomes (-3, 6).

questions.questionText: Point A is at (3, 5). It is translated 1 unit left and 2 units down. What are the coordinates of A'?
questions.explanation: A translation adds the horizontal change to x and the vertical change to y: (3, 5) becomes (2, 3).

questions.questionText: Point A is at (-2, -4). It is translated 6 units right and 1 unit up. What are the coordinates of A'?
questions.explanation: A translation adds the horizontal change to x and the vertical change to y: (-2, -4) becomes (4, -3).

questions.questionText: A point moves from (-4, 1) to (2, 5). Which translation vector describes the movement?
questions.explanation: Subtract starting coordinates from ending coordinates: 2 - -4 = 6 and 5 - 1 = 4.

questions.questionText: A point moves from (3, -2) to (-5, 4). Which translation vector describes the movement?
questions.explanation: Subtract starting coordinates from ending coordinates: -5 - 3 = -8 and 4 - -2 = 6.

questions.questionText: A point moves from (0, 0) to (6, -3). Which translation vector describes the movement?
questions.explanation: Subtract starting coordinates from ending coordinates: 6 - 0 = 6 and -3 - 0 = -3.

questions.questionText: A point moves from (-7, -3) to (1, 6). Which translation vector describes the movement?
questions.explanation: Subtract starting coordinates from ending coordinates: 1 - -7 = 8 and 6 - -3 = 9.

questions.questionText: A point moves from (5, 2) to (-4, -5). Which translation vector describes the movement?
questions.explanation: Subtract starting coordinates from ending coordinates: -4 - 5 = -9 and -5 - 2 = -7.

questions.questionText: Which coordinate rule translates every point 7 units right and 2 units down?
questions.explanation: A translation changes x by the horizontal move and y by the vertical move, so the rule is (x + 7, y - 2).

questions.questionText: Which coordinate rule translates every point 3 units left and 6 units up?
questions.explanation: A translation changes x by the horizontal move and y by the vertical move, so the rule is (x - 3, y + 6).

questions.questionText: Which coordinate rule translates every point 4 units right and no vertical move?
questions.explanation: A translation changes x by the horizontal move and y by the vertical move, so the rule is (x + 4, y).

questions.questionText: Which coordinate rule translates every point no horizontal move and 5 units down?
questions.explanation: A translation changes x by the horizontal move and y by the vertical move, so the rule is (x, y - 5).

questions.questionText: Which coordinate rule translates every point 6 units left and 1 unit down?
questions.explanation: A translation changes x by the horizontal move and y by the vertical move, so the rule is (x - 6, y - 1).

questions.questionText: After a translation by vector <6, 2>, point A' is (4, -1). Where was point A before the translation?
questions.explanation: To work backward, subtract the translation vector from the image point: (4, -1) - <6, 2> = (-2, -3).

questions.questionText: After a translation by vector <-2, -5>, point A' is (-3, 7). Where was point A before the translation?
questions.explanation: To work backward, subtract the translation vector from the image point: (-3, 7) - <-2, -5> = (-1, 12).

questions.questionText: After a translation by vector <0, 4>, point A' is (5, 5). Where was point A before the translation?
questions.explanation: To work backward, subtract the translation vector from the image point: (5, 5) - <0, 4> = (5, 1).

questions.questionText: After a translation by vector <3, -3>, point A' is (-6, 2). Where was point A before the translation?
questions.explanation: To work backward, subtract the translation vector from the image point: (-6, 2) - <3, -3> = (-9, 5).

questions.questionText: After a translation by vector <-4, 1>, point A' is (1, -8). Where was point A before the translation?
questions.explanation: To work backward, subtract the translation vector from the image point: (1, -8) - <-4, 1> = (5, -9).

questions.questionText: Segment AB has endpoints A(-2, 1) and B(3, 1). Translate the segment by vector <4, -3>. What are A' and B'?
questions.explanation: Translate each endpoint by the same vector <4, -3>. The size and direction of the segment do not change.

questions.questionText: Segment AB has endpoints A(0, -4) and B(0, 2). Translate the segment by vector <-5, 1>. What are A' and B'?
questions.explanation: Translate each endpoint by the same vector <-5, 1>. The size and direction of the segment do not change.

questions.questionText: Segment AB has endpoints A(-6, -2) and B(-1, 3). Translate the segment by vector <2, 4>. What are A' and B'?
questions.explanation: Translate each endpoint by the same vector <2, 4>. The size and direction of the segment do not change.

questions.questionText: Segment AB has endpoints A(2, 5) and B(6, 5). Translate the segment by vector <-3, -6>. What are A' and B'?
questions.explanation: Translate each endpoint by the same vector <-3, -6>. The size and direction of the segment do not change.

questions.questionText: Segment AB has endpoints A(-4, 0) and B(1, -2). Translate the segment by vector <5, 2>. What are A' and B'?
questions.explanation: Translate each endpoint by the same vector <5, 2>. The size and direction of the segment do not change.

questions.questionText: A student translated (-2, 3) by vector <5, -4> and got (3, 7). What is the correct image point?
questions.explanation: The correct image is (3, -1). The shown work is off because it added 4 instead of subtracting 4 from the y-coordinate.

questions.questionText: A student translated (6, -1) by vector <-3, 2> and got (9, 1). What is the correct image point?
questions.explanation: The correct image is (3, 1). The shown work is off because it moved right 3 instead of left 3.

questions.questionText: A student translated (0, -5) by vector <4, 6> and got (6, -1). What is the correct image point?
questions.explanation: The correct image is (4, 1). The shown work is off because it switched the horizontal and vertical changes.

questions.questionText: A student translated (-7, 4) by vector <2, -5> and got (-5, -4). What is the correct image point?
questions.explanation: The correct image is (-5, -1). The shown work is off because it subtracted 5 from the wrong starting y-coordinate.

questions.questionText: A student translated (3, 2) by vector <-6, -3> and got (-3, 5). What is the correct image point?
questions.explanation: The correct image is (-3, -1). The shown work is off because it moved up 3 instead of down 3.

questions.questionText: Point P(1, -2) is translated by <3, 5> and then by <-4, 2>. Where is the final image point?
questions.explanation: Combine the two translations: <3, 5> + <-4, 2> = <-1, 7>. Then add that vector to P.

questions.questionText: Point P(-5, 4) is translated by <6, -1> and then by <2, -7>. Where is the final image point?
questions.explanation: Combine the two translations: <6, -1> + <2, -7> = <8, -8>. Then add that vector to P.

questions.questionText: Point P(0, 3) is translated by <-2, -6> and then by <5, 1>. Where is the final image point?
questions.explanation: Combine the two translations: <-2, -6> + <5, 1> = <3, -5>. Then add that vector to P.

questions.questionText: Point P(7, -4) is translated by <-3, 3> and then by <-5, 6>. Where is the final image point?
questions.explanation: Combine the two translations: <-3, 3> + <-5, 6> = <-8, 9>. Then add that vector to P.

questions.questionText: Point P(-1, -1) is translated by <4, 0> and then by <-6, -2>. Where is the final image point?
questions.explanation: Combine the two translations: <4, 0> + <-6, -2> = <-2, -2>. Then add that vector to P.

questions.questionText: Segment AB goes from A(-3, 2) to B(1, 2). After translating by <5, -1>, what must stay true about the segment?
options: The translated segment has run 9 and rise -1.
The translated segment has run 0 and rise 4.
The translated segment has the same run 4 and rise 0.
The translated segment has the opposite run -4 and opposite rise 0.
questions.correctAnswer: The translated segment has the same run 4 and rise 0.
questions.explanation: A translation slides every point the same distance and direction, so lengths, slopes, runs, and rises stay unchanged.

questions.questionText: Segment AB goes from A(2, -4) to B(2, 3). After translating by <-6, 2>, what must stay true about the segment?
options: The translated segment has run -6 and rise 9.
The translated segment has the same run 0 and rise 7.
The translated segment has run 7 and rise 0.
The translated segment has the opposite run 0 and opposite rise -7.
questions.correctAnswer: The translated segment has the same run 0 and rise 7.
questions.explanation: A translation slides every point the same distance and direction, so lengths, slopes, runs, and rises stay unchanged.

questions.questionText: Segment AB goes from A(-5, -5) to B(0, -1). After translating by <3, 4>, what must stay true about the segment?
options: The translated segment has run 8 and rise 8.
The translated segment has run 4 and rise 5.
The translated segment has the same run 5 and rise 4.
The translated segment has the opposite run -5 and opposite rise -4.
questions.correctAnswer: The translated segment has the same run 5 and rise 4.
questions.explanation: A translation slides every point the same distance and direction, so lengths, slopes, runs, and rises stay unchanged.

questions.questionText: Segment AB goes from A(4, 1) to B(7, 6). After translating by <-2, -3>, what must stay true about the segment?
options: The translated segment has run 1 and rise 2.
The translated segment has the same run 3 and rise 5.
The translated segment has run 5 and rise 3.
The translated segment has the opposite run -3 and opposite rise -5.
questions.correctAnswer: The translated segment has the same run 3 and rise 5.
questions.explanation: A translation slides every point the same distance and direction, so lengths, slopes, runs, and rises stay unchanged.

questions.questionText: Segment AB goes from A(-1, 5) to B(5, 1). After translating by <-4, 0>, what must stay true about the segment?
options: The translated segment has run 2 and rise -4.
The translated segment has run -4 and rise 6.
The translated segment has the same run 6 and rise -4.
The translated segment has the opposite run -6 and opposite rise 4.
questions.correctAnswer: The translated segment has the same run 6 and rise -4.
questions.explanation: A translation slides every point the same distance and direction, so lengths, slopes, runs, and rises stay unchanged.

questions.questionText: A translation sends point A(2, 7) to A'(-3, 8). Which rule would move A' back to A?
questions.explanation: The reverse translation uses the opposite vector. Since A moved by <-5, 1>, A' moves back by <5, -1>.

questions.questionText: A translation sends point A(-4, 3) to A'(2, 1). Which rule would move A' back to A?
questions.explanation: The reverse translation uses the opposite vector. Since A moved by <6, -2>, A' moves back by <-6, 2>.

questions.questionText: A translation sends point A(0, -6) to A'(-3, -10). Which rule would move A' back to A?
questions.explanation: The reverse translation uses the opposite vector. Since A moved by <-3, -4>, A' moves back by <3, 4>.

questions.questionText: A translation sends point A(5, 5) to A'(6, -2). Which rule would move A' back to A?
questions.explanation: The reverse translation uses the opposite vector. Since A moved by <1, -7>, A' moves back by <-1, 7>.

questions.questionText: A translation sends point A(-7, -2) to A'(-3, 1). Which rule would move A' back to A?
questions.explanation: The reverse translation uses the opposite vector. Since A moved by <4, 3>, A' moves back by <-4, -3>.
